source: Codex authored in response to the RAL system experiment request, 2026-09-21
task: Clean the rail, install carriage, end stop, two pins and handle, then verify bidirectional stroke and retained pins.
grounding: Use current RGB-D object heights for transport clearance, detector residual for contact speed, and observed source distance for pin order. Cartesian targets are resolved by existing perception/planning skills.

strategies.name: adaptive_base
strategies.rationale: Use observed clearance and uncertainty with the nearer supply pin first.

strategies.name: alternate_order
strategies.rationale: Change intermediate robot configuration and the order of fixture loading.

strategies.name: slow_contact
strategies.rationale: Reduce contact motion speed when pin seating or fixture motion is uncertain.

strategies.name: firm_grip
strategies.rationale: Increase pin grasp force to resist slip during transport.

strategies.name: gentle_grip
strategies.rationale: Reduce gripping force to avoid excessive contact loading.

strategies.name: high_pin_grasp
strategies.rationale: Change finger clearance near the pin holder and guide.

strategies.name: high_transport
strategies.rationale: Increase transfer height above the observed supply layout.

strategies.name: low_transport
strategies.rationale: Use a lower route to change arm configuration and path length.

strategies.name: slow_stop_seating
strategies.rationale: Seat the fixture slowly to improve the downstream hole state.

strategies.name: alternate_wipe
strategies.rationale: Traverse the same cleaning region from the opposite direction.

strategies.name: cross_handle_grasp
strategies.rationale: Change the handle approach direction when the fixture restricts finger access.

strategies.name: cross_first_pin_grasp
strategies.rationale: Change the first pin approach direction to alter holder exit motion.
